newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's YUKOS to vote on control by Menatep ally.
newsitem.headline: Russia's YUKOS to vote on control by Menatep ally.

text.p: Russian oil company YUKOS will hold an extraordinary shareholders meeting on February 19 to decide whether or not to transfer administrative control to Bank Menatep's industrial holding company, a YUKOS spokesman said on Monday.
"The idea is outside control by Rosprom," YUKOS spokesman Alexei Gorshkov told Reuters, referring to a company that administers more than 30 companies controlled by Menatep.
He said that YUKOS had already consolidated control over its units.
Menatep said there was no direct relationship between Menatep and Monblan, but Russian commercial banks have used front companies to control companies won in government auctions in the past.

At the time of the shares-for-loans auction, Laguna also won an investment tender for a 33.3 percent stake in YUKOS, subsequently diluted to about 24 percent. That was subsequently transferred to several companies whose ownership is unclear, but which have been backed by Menatep in other transactions.

YUKOS is one of a dozen vertically integrated oil companies established by Russia after the breakup of the Soviet Union. Its main operating unit is Yuganskneftegaz, which may have the largest oil reserves in the world.
